purpose: Separate predicting consequences of a specified edit from proposing a repair for an independent demand; do not mistake a developer's chosen patch for the set of necessary repairs.

sources.scope: CIA survey Table III: dependency, repository, coupling and execution information; hybrid analyses
Cai and Santelices 2015 sections 3.1, 5.2, 5.3: PI/EAS predicts method impact from prechange enter/return-into events; execution differencing for observed ground truth under same tests
Posnett et al. sections 6.4–6.5: incremental R-squared for class role given size and release below 2 percentage points in examined pattern/project combinations; size may mediate, not causal null

A.input: specified edit location and transformation, frozen base source and tests
A.oracle: paired execution differencing for fixed edit and test inputs; unobserved effects UNKNOWN

B.input: frozen source, independent demand, rights, existing contracts, common evidence budget
B.output: candidate repair menu and predicted admissibility/cost
B.oracle: independently verified bounded candidate execution, not unique maintainer patch
comparators: equal-information ordinary semantic analysis and search

A: analysis time and information acquisition cost
B: validated candidate coverage within declared grammar
separate actual measured costs from proxy counts

controls: same prechange tests and source visibility
do not expose changed traces to prospective predictors
runtime coverage does not prove global absence
size-only baseline for change-proneness; do not condition on post-intervention size for total causal effect
no score promotion from Click already inspected calibration
stop: If conventional semantic analysis matches on same information, retain tie; only extend when a discriminating out-of-sample question is available.
